newsitem.title: CYPRUS: IMF satisfied with Cyprus, finance minister says.
newsitem.headline: IMF satisfied with Cyprus, finance minister says.

text.p: International Monetary Fund officials on a fact-finding mission in Cyprus have expressed satisfaction at the economic performance of the island, Finance Minister Christodoulos Christodoulou said on Monday.

"The fund now considers that Cyprus has reached the point where it does not need the help and guidance to the extent other countries need it, like central and Eastern European countries," Christodoulou told reporters.
Christodoulou, speaking to reporters after meeting the IMF team, said they were given a general overview of the performance of the economy in 1996 and of prospects for 1997.
The IMF team plans meetings with representatives of the finance ministry and the central bank.

"They wanted to be briefed on the intentions of the government concerning the deregulation of the monetary system and put issues relating to the modernisation of semi-government organisations," said Christodoulou.
He was referring to the deregulation of services, such as telecommunications, where semi-government organisations currently hold a monopoly.
The government says it is committed to deregulating its monetary system, still under tight legislative control, by the end of 1997 or the very beginning of 1998.

Removal of restrictions on foreign exchange movement, with a parallel drive to deregulate interest rate ceilings, is expected after consultation with all parties concerned. Interest rate ceilings are currently set by law at nine percent.
Christodoulou said the fact that the IMF team was small indicated the island no longer had to be as closely scrutinised as in previous years.

Budget figures presented to parliament by Christodoulou last week forecast a fiscal deficit of 175 million pounds ($371.8 million) in 1997, or 4 percent of GDP, representing a rise of almost 14 percent compared with a deficit of 120 million pounds in 1996.
Nominal GDP growth will reach 3.5 percent in 1997 from 2.5 expected this year. Unemployment is expected to be 2.9 percent, a slight drop from this year's expected 3.0 percent.
Inflation in 1997 is expected to be about 2.8 percent compared to 3.0 percent expected this year.
Cyprus hopes to start accession talks with the European Union by mid-1998 and has launched a drive to harmonise its economy with that of the trade bloc.

The island is still divided, with the north occupied by Turkey since an invasion in 1974 which was sparked by a coup attempt in Nicosia, engineered by the then military government in Greece. ($=0.47 cents)
